topicTitle: Scalar and vector quantities, types of vectors; addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors
notes: **Scalar vs vector:** scalars have magnitude only (mass, temperature); vectors have magnitude and direction (displacement, force).

**Types of vectors:** equal vectors (same magnitude and direction), opposite vectors (same magnitude, opposite direction), unit vector (magnitude 1), null vector (magnitude 0), parallel vectors, collinear vectors, coplanar vectors.
**Addition:** $\vec{a} + \vec{b} = \vec{b} + \vec{a}$ (commutative). Triangle law: place tail of $\vec{b}$ at head of $\vec{a}$; resultant closes the triangle.

**Subtraction:** $\vec{a} - \vec{b} = \vec{a} + (-\vec{b})$. Geometrically, draw $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ from same point; $\vec{a} - \vec{b}$ is the vector from head of $\vec{b}$ to head of $\vec{a}$.
**Scalar multiplication:** $k\vec{a}$ has magnitude $|k|\cdot|\vec{a}|$. If $k>0$, direction unchanged; if $k<0$, direction reversed; if $k=0$, null vector.
